title: model-loader Profile
description: JSON schema for a model-loader backend profile. Each profile is persisted as a single .json file under the configured profiles directory (default: ~/.config/model-loader/profiles/).

schemaVersion.description: Profile JSON schema version. Always 3 for the current format.

id.description: Unique filename-safe identifier for the profile. Used as the filename (id.json). Must be lowercase ASCII alphanumeric groups separated by single '.', '_', or '-'. Auto-generated from name via Slugify when not provided.

name.description: Human-readable profile name. Displayed in the TUI.

description.description: Optional free-text description of the profile.

tags.description: Optional list of string tags for filtering and grouping in the UI.

model.description: Model selector for the profile's backend. For local-file backends (for example llama-server) an absolute or relative path to the model file (typically a .gguf file); existence is checked at profile create/edit time, not only at launch. The lmstudio backend accepts a daemon-side model key instead of a path (no existence check). The vllm, sglang, unsloth, and freetoken backends also accept a Hugging Face repo ID (for example meta-llama/Llama-3-8B).

args.description: Structured backend command-line flags as key/value pairs. Each key is a flag name in canonical long form (e.g. 'ctx-size', 'flash-attn'). Values must match the type declared in the backend's FlagSchema (bool, int, float, or string). Note: due to JSON round-tripping, integer values may deserialize as float64; the validator accepts whole-number floats as integers. 'port' is reserved: it is assigned automatically by the process manager; if present in a profile it is ignored and stripped on load/save.

anyOf.description: FlagTypeFloat: floating-point values (e.g. temp, top-p, defrag-thold). Accepts both integers and floats.
FlagTypeString: free-text values (e.g. cache-type-k, host). FlagTypeEnum values are also strings restricted to a fixed set validated against the backend schema's EnumValues.

extraArgs.description: Raw extra CLI arguments passed as-is to the backend binary. Each entry must start with '--'. Format: '--flag' or '--flag=value'. For non-bool flags without '=' the next array element is consumed as the value.

defaultBackground.description: If true, the process starts in background mode by default when launched from the TUI.

logFilePath.description: Optional custom log file path for this profile's backend output. Falls back to global log directory if empty.

backendId.description: Optional ID of the backend (from the backend catalog) to use for launching this profile. If empty, the default backend from the catalog is used.

env.description: Optional environment variables applied to the backend process at launch. Keys must match [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*. Last value wins on duplicate keys.

llamaServerBinaryPath.description: LEGACY: read-only migration field. Not written after migration. Use the backend catalog instead.

restart_policy.description: Restart policy for the backend process. '' or 'none' = never restart, 'on-failure' = restart only on non-zero exit, 'always' = restart unconditionally. An empty string is treated as 'none'.

max_restarts.description: Maximum number of restart attempts. Only applies when restart_policy is 'on-failure' or 'always'.

backoff_seconds.description: Delay in seconds between restart attempts.

meta.description: System-managed metadata. Populated automatically by the store on create/update.

createdAt.description: ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 timestamp when the profile was first created.

updatedAt.description: ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 timestamp when the profile was last modified.

lastUsedAt.description: Optional ISO 8601 timestamp of the most recent launch. Null or absent if never launched.

pinned.description: If true, the profile is pinned to the top of the profile list in the TUI.

envVar.description: A single KEY=VALUE environment variable applied to the backend process at launch.

value.description: Environment variable value. Used literally (no shell expansion).

flagTypeNote.description: Flag value type semantics: boolean -> FlagTypeBool, integer -> FlagTypeInt, number -> FlagTypeFloat, string -> FlagTypeString or FlagTypeEnum. Enum flags are represented as strings restricted to a fixed set of values, validated against the backend schema's EnumValues.

argsExample.description: Example args block for a typical llama-server profile.

extraArgsExample.description: Example extraArgs demonstrating both inline-value and next-element value styles.
